statement: If a straight line falling on two straight lines make the alternate angles equal to one another, the straight lines will be parallel to one another.
heath_proof: For let the straight line EF falling on the two straightlines AB, CD make the alternate angles AEF, EFD equal to one another; I say that AB is parallel to CD. For, if not, AB, CD when produced will meet either in the directionof B, D or towards A, C. Let them be produced and meet, in the direction of B, D, at G. Then, in the triangle GEF, the exterior angle AEF is equal to the interior and oppositeangle EFG: which is impossible. [I. 16] Therefore AB, CD when produced will not meet in the direction of B, D. Similarly it can be proved that neither will they meettowards A, C. But straight lines which do not meet in either direction are parallel; [Def. 23] therefore AB is parallel to CD.
ai_proof_text:
1.27
**Statement:** If a straight line falling on two straight lines make the alternate angles equal to one another, the straight lines will be parallel to one another.

**Step 1.** Let the straight line EF fall on the two straight lines AB and CD, making the alternate angles AEH and GHD equal, where E is the point of intersection with AB and H is the point of intersection with CD. We are to prove that AB is parallel to CD.

**Step 2.** Suppose AB is not parallel to CD. Then, by the definition of parallel lines (D1.23), the lines AB and CD, when produced, will meet on one side or the other.

**Step 3.** Suppose they meet at a point K on the side of B and D when produced. Then E, H, and K form a triangle EHK.

**Step 4.** In triangle EHK, the angle AEH is an exterior angle, since it is formed by side EH of the triangle and the extension EA of side EK beyond vertex E. The angle EHK is an interior and opposite angle of this triangle.

**Step 5.** By Proposition 1.16, the exterior angle of any triangle is greater than either of the interior and opposite angles. Therefore angle AEH is greater than angle EHK.

**Step 6.** But angle EHK is the same as angle GHD (since K lies on the extension of CD beyond H in the direction of D, making angle EHK and angle GHD the same angle, or equivalently K is on ray HD so angle EHK = angle GHD). Therefore angle AEH is greater than angle GHD.

**Step 7.** This contradicts the hypothesis that angle AEH equals angle GHD. Therefore AB and CD do not meet on the side of B and D.

**Step 8.** By an entirely symmetric argument, if AB and CD were to meet on the side of A and C at some point K', then in triangle EHK', the angle GHD would be an exterior angle and angle HEA' (i.e., angle BEH, which equals angle AEH's supplement's complement — more precisely, angle DHK' = angle GHD is exterior to triangle EHK' while angle HEK' is interior and opposite). Applying 1.16 again, angle GHD would be greater than angle HEK', that is, greater than angle AEH (since angle HEK' = angle AEH as K' lies on ray EA). This again contradicts the hypothesis that these alternate angles are equal.

**Step 9.** Since AB and CD do not meet when produced in either direction, they are parallel by the definition of parallel lines (D1.23).

**Step 10.** Therefore, if a straight line falling on two straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one another, the straight lines are parallel to one another. Q.E.D.
